title: Decision matrix + ops constraints for private deployment TCO
content:
Purpose:
A pragmatic decision matrix + ops constraint checklist to help Solutions Engineering and Sales quickly evaluate private deployment options (on-prem vs VPC) and recommend licensing + support bundles that minimize TCO surprises for mid-market and enterprise buyers. This is explicitly a working artifact — lean, action-oriented, and intended to be copied into customer-tailored notes.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
When comparing on-prem and VPC private deployments, the dominant TCO drivers are hardware amortization, networking egress/latency costs, managed vs customer ops headcount, and support SLAs that affect incident recovery windows. For customers with stable 24/7 inference (high token volumes, latency-sensitive), Dedicated hardware amortized with Redwood-managed bundles typically yields lower operational overhead. For bursty or heavily regulated customers, on-prem plus premium support can make sense if the customer already has racks and staff. The decision matrix below prioritizes three quick triggers (hardware footprint, data residency, ops maturity) followed by sensitivity knobs (utilization, model mix, VL cache hit rate).

Assumptions used in the quick model (baseline):
- Hardware list price (top-end GPU node): $46,000 per 8x A100-like configuration; effective amortized cost: 36 months, straight-line.
- Typical rack-level baseline: 6 nodes (48 GPUs) for a medium enterprise workload.
- VPC instance equivalent (managed host) markup: 1.45x of on-prem amortized HW cost (includes infra maintenance + network premium).
- Redwood Private license: one-time platform fee $120k + per-node license $1,200/mo.
- Support bundles: Standard (included, 9–5 business), Premium ($25k/yr, 24/7 with 1-hr incident response), Enterprise ($85k/yr, 30-minute response + on-call rotation).
- Ops headcount: customer-managed ops cost $140k/yr per FTE fully loaded; Redwood managed ops removes need for 0.5–2.0 FTE depending on bundle.
- Model mix baseline: 60% generation (latency-sensitive), 40% embeddings/batch.
- Utilization sensitivity: low 20%, medium 55%, high 80% (of theoretical token throughput).

Decision matrix (quick, tick-box logic):
- Trigger 1: Data residency/compliance prohibits cloud control plane? -> Prefer on-prem or VPC with private control plane.
- Trigger 2: Sustained high throughput (>20B tokens/month) and latency SLA <100ms? -> Prefer dedicated capacity or on-prem hardware with Redwood-managed runtime.
- Trigger 3: Customer ops maturity below 1 SRE focused on ML infra? -> Prefer Redwood-managed VPC or Dedicated + premium support.
- Trigger 4: Customer wants full air-gap/physical custody? -> On-prem with Enterprise support.

Mini-sensitivity table (illustrative — use for rapid whiteboarding):
Columns: Scenario | Hardware amort (36m) | License (annualized) | Support | Ops FTE cost | Net annual delta (VPC vs on-prem)
- Baseline (medium util 55%): On-prem annualized HW = $92k; License annualized = $14.4k; Support (Premium) = $25k; Ops FTE (0.8 FTE) = $112k. VPC replacement = HW*1.45 + managed ops fee (equiv) -> net +$48k vs on-prem.
- Low-util (20%): On-prem under-utilized -> ops fixed costs dominate; VPC often cheaper by $85k/yr due to capacity pooling.
- High-util (80%): On-prem amortization wins; VPC premium becomes relatively smaller -> on-prem cheaper by $60k/yr.

Key heuristics for Recommendations (short actionable bullets):
- If util <30% and customer lacks spare rack/headcount: recommend VPC with Standard+Premium support; show clear delta vs on-prem.
- If util >65% and customer can supply colo + power: model on-prem 36–48 month amortization and pitch a License + Enterprise Support bundle.
- If latency SLA <75ms and cross-region failover not required: prefer on-prem or colo with local region VPC peering.
- If the customer requires audit logs/KMS in their HSM: include Private deployment (customer-managed KMS) + add-on compliance package (estimate +$18k/yr).

Ops constraints checklist (for solutions calls):
- Power/cooling available at planned colo? (Y/N) -> if N, discount on-prem viability.
- Network egress patterns (tokens in/out) and peering latency requirements. Capture sample p95 latency for 100k qps synthetic test.
- Capacity headroom needed for failover (N% extra). Default recommend 30% standby capacity for HA.
- Patch/upgrade windows tolerated by customer (weekly/biweekly/monthly). If weekly-patch policy -> Redwood-managed automations recommended.
- Disaster recovery RTO/RPO requirements. If RTO <1h, recommend Enterprise support + cross-region replication.

Live calculation sketch (cells you'd paste into a quick Google Sheet):
- A1: Nodes_needed (user input) = 6
- A2: GPU_cost_per_node = 46000
- A3: Amort_months = 36
- A4: Annual_hw = Nodes_needed * GPU_cost_per_node * 12 / Amort_months
- A5: License_monthly_per_node = 1200
- A6: Annual_license = Nodes_needed * License_monthly_per_node * 12
- A7: Support_annual = pick(standard=0, premium=25000, enterprise=85000)
- A8: Ops_ftes = pick(redwood-managed=0.2, customer=0.8..1.6) * fte_cost(140000)
- A9: VPC_markup = 1.45
- A10: VPC_equivalent = Annual_hw * VPC_markup + managed_ops_fee_est
- A11: Net_delta = VPC_equivalent - (Annual_hw + Annual_license + Support_annual + Ops_ftes)

Red flags to call out on sales decks (things that blow up TCO quickly):
- Model churn: frequent large model swaps cause repeat optimization & quantization cycles; add $Xk/yr service line item.
- Cache miss rates above 40% for prefix-cached workloads -> token costs spike nonlinearly.
- Unexpected egress between zones/regions for multimodal pipelines -> network billing large.
- Security/regulatory audits that require dedicated logging retention >5yrs -> storage and legal hold costs.

Customer conversation scripts (copyable snippets):
- When customer is ops-light: "From a TCO standpoint, if your average utilization is under ~30% we usually see our VPC customers save on operational overhead — we can run a quick model with your monthly token figures to show the break-even."
- When customer has racks and stable loads: "Given you already own rack space and have on-call SREs, the on-prem amortization often becomes favorable after year one; we can show a 3-year blended TCO that includes support and a license."

Immediate next steps (for the SE owner on the opportunity):
1) Fill the mini-sheet above with customer-specific inputs (tokens/mo, model mix, downtime cost per hour, colo power price).
2) Run 3 sensitivity runs: low/medium/high utilization and low/high cache hit rate.
3) Attach the result to the opportunity and propose a mixed recommendation (e.g., start VPC + migrate to on-prem at commit threshold X).
4) If customer requires air-gap, route to Private Deployment engineering for feasibility; capture estimated integration effort in story points.

Appendix: Quick example outputs (toy numbers) — use for demos only:
- Customer A (mid-market SaaS, tokens 12B/mo; util est 60%): On-prem 3-year blended cost = $1.22M, VPC = $1.36M, Delta = on-prem -$140k over 3 yrs -> recommend on-prem with Redwood managed ops + Premium Support.
- Customer B (regulated fintech, tokens 4B/mo; util est 25%): On-prem 3-year blended = $460k, VPC = $385k -> recommend VPC with Private control plane + Standard support; discuss compliance add-on.

Notes / open questions to resolve before finalizing for GTM templates:
- Need a standard "managed ops fee" table for VPC that maps to normalized FTE offsets (so sales can quote quickly).
- Confirm current licensed node monthly pricing (last update 2025-06 was provisional).
- Add precise network egress estimator for multimodal workloads (images + text) — engineering input needed.

Owners / reviewers: Aisha (author), Marco (cost model), Liang (infra constraints), Sophie (sales messaging).
